criteria: Preserve visually distinct neutral macro-phenotypes without requiring every subdivision to define a new macroregion.
Separate blank, background, and section-edge appearances from pale low-cellularity tissue.
Retain cellular variation reproduced across anonymized Slides A-H, assessed using centroid, per-slide, mid/random, and low-margin exemplars together with anonymous spatial maps and composition plots.
metadata.review_scope: Blinded technical visual review of candidate K=3 through K=9 for the joint eight-WSI run, using only the anonymized exemplar atlases, spatial heatmaps, composition plots, lineage/summary visuals, and internal candidate metrics supplied for this run.
metadata.blinding_limitation: Only anonymized run materials were reviewed. This is a technical non-pathologist assessment based on neutral visual morphology and is not a diagnostic interpretation.
metadata.joint_run_note: The anonymized spatial maps show that Slides A-D and Slides E-H are largely described by different cellular clusters. This representation split is recorded as an observation about the joint run; it is not interpreted here, and cluster IDs remain strictly run-local.

candidates.qualitative_notes: C0 is a dense cellular class present only on Slides A-D and C1 a second cellular class present on all eight slides. C2 pools clearly different appearances in a single class: near-blank background, a linear foreign-fibre artefact, pale pink amorphous granular low-nuclear material, thin sparse tissue strands, and cellular low-margin fields. Blank/background, section-edge strands, and pale low-cellularity material are all merged, so the neutral macro-phenotypes are not preserved.

C0, C1 and C3 give three reproducible cellular appearances, but C2 continues to pool near-blank background, the fibre artefact, pale pink amorphous material and thin sparse strands across its centroid, per-slide and mid/random examples. The principal blank versus section-edge versus pale low-cellularity distinctions all remain merged in one class.

C2 now isolates a clean near-blank background class, which is a genuine improvement over K=4. However C3 still pools thin sparse tissue strands and section-edge fragments together with pale pink amorphous granular low-nuclear material in its centroid, per-slide and mid/random examples. Section-edge and pale low-cellularity appearances therefore remain merged, so the stated separation criterion is not yet met.

C3 is a clean near-blank background class and the cellular compartment gains a further subdivision (C0, C1, C2, C5). C4 nevertheless still combines sparse strand/boundary tissue with pale pink amorphous granular material, reproducing the K=5 limitation. The additional class was spent on cellular tissue rather than on resolving the remaining merged non-cellular macro-phenotype.

K=7 is the first candidate that separates all three non-cellular macro-phenotypes: C3 is near-blank background, C4 is sparse strand and section-edge tissue with scattered nuclei, and C5 (n=732) is a distinct pale pink amorphous granular class containing degenerate or fragmented nuclear debris, present on seven of the eight slides. C0, C1, C2 and C6 retain the cellular variation, with C0/C1 confined to Slides A-D and C2/C6 spanning all eight. The anonymous spatial maps show contiguous coherent regions for every class, including large coherent pale-amorphous territories on individual slides.

All macro-phenotype separations from K=7 persist: C4 near-blank background, C5 sparse strand/boundary tissue, and C6 (n=699) pale amorphous granular material. The extra class further subdivides the cellular compartment (C0, C1, C2, C3, C7). This adds granularity to already separated phenotypes rather than recovering a new one.

Separation is retained and the background compartment itself splits into a uniformly blank class (C3, n=634) and a blank-with-specks/debris class (C7, n=1043), alongside sparse strands (C5) and pale amorphous material (C6). The cellular compartment is subdivided into C0, C1, C2, C4 and C8. As at K=8, the additional classes refine existing appearances rather than exposing a new reproducible macro-phenotype.
